03-pelican.name: Halcyon
03-pelican.pitch: Mid-century paperback method (Tschichold's bands, Marber's grid, Facetti's abstract science covers) without the pastiche. Every cover has the same three bands: title on paper, a black level strip, and a flat colour field holding one abstract emblem of the book's mechanism. Field colour is the level (yellow, green, ultramarine), and signal red marks the idea.

06-letterform.name: Codepoint
06-letterform.pitch: One book, one character. Each title gets a single glyph from its own subject (∂ for the maths, σ for neural networks, ≈ for context compaction, QKᵀ for transformers), set monumental and cropped above a fixed rule, with the title hung below like a type-specimen caption. Level is how much ink the cover carries: bare paper, ultramarine, then black.

10-wildcard.name: Some Assembly Required
10-wildcard.pitch: Vizuara is a library for building things, and half its titles end in “from Scratch”, so every book is a model kit. Each emblem is an injection-moulded parts tree (a sprue) built from the book's own mechanism: an H-tree runner feeding 32 GPUs for 5D Parallelism, weights as runners for Neural Networks. Card colour and skill-level pips show level, plastic colour shows series, and kit numbers VZ-001 to VZ-052 make the shelf collectable.

01-grid.name: Figure/Ground
01-grid.pitch: One 12 × 15 module grid, one typeface and three inks for every book. Level picks the ground (paper, signal red, black), so a shelf reads as a gradient of difficulty. Each book stands one figure built from squares, circles and bars on that grid, taken from its own mechanism: a GPT's causal mask, a 5D device mesh, an ODE direction field. A notched bookmark ribbon is the imprint, and its length also encodes level.

04-drafting.name: Drawing Office
04-drafting.pitch: Every book is issued as an engineering drawing of the machine it teaches you to build. The brand lives in the title block: drawing number, level stamped in ink squares, capsules and hours as the extent, units (“Tokens”, “GPUs”), and Vizuara as the issuing office. Each cover uses a different real drafting view (section, isometric, detail, break) on one paper, one graphite and one engineering-red ink.

05-algorithmic.name: Figure 0
05-algorithmic.pitch: Every cover is one run of the book's own algorithm, computed in the page from a seed. Gradient descent draws the maths book, a network trained in the browser draws Neural Networks, and a simulated pipeline schedule draws 5D Parallelism. The FIG. 0 caption states exactly what ran, with numbers read back from that run. Ground darkens with level: paper, signal red, carbon.

07-riso.name: Overprint
07-riso.pitch: Every book looks pulled off a risograph: natural paper, two or three real riso inks that overprint, halftone screens made in code, and drums slightly out of register. The idea usually lives where the inks cross: the overprint is the GEMM output tile, the SQL join, the part of the context the model actually sees. Level is a ski-run mark (circle, square, diamond) in the key ink.

09-atlas.name: Interchange
09-atlas.pitch: Each book is a Beck/Vignelli transit map of its own subject. Its parts are the lines and each capsule is one tick, checked against the real capsule counts, so the 69-capsule DSA book coils into a long spiral while the 9-capsule book is tiny. The key at the foot doubles as a table of contents. Beginner and intermediate books are pale day maps, advanced books are dark night maps.

02-plates.name: Specimen Plates
02-plates.pitch: Every book is a numbered plate in one atlas of machine learning: a single engraved specimen of its actual mechanism, lettered a, b, c with an italic legend, the way Gray or Haeckel documented theirs. The drawings are computed, not decorated (descent paths integrated on the real surface, the real 2⁵ device mesh). Paper tone gives level: sage, Ingres blue, sanguine. Everything prints as one spot tint plus black.
